terms.comment: A document from a magistrate assuring its holder some right or favour (Lewis & Short); in Pliny’s letters to Trajan, the permits for travelling by the public post. Traupman uses it for a driving licence (see driving licence); the passport is commeātūs diplōma (see passport).

terms.gloss: leave, permission; in Neo-Latin a licence
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.103: puerīs nōn omnem lūdendī licentiam damus
M-O s.v. driver’s license; city council
terms.comment: Classically the freedom to do as one pleases, given or taken, and often too much of it (Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens records it for a licence in Neo-Latin: licentiam ad tabernam coffeāriam condendam, a licence to open a coffee house (Trappen, 1843).

phrases.latin: Diplōmata, quōrum praeteritus est diēs, nōn dēbent esse in ūsū.
phrases.english: Permits whose date has passed should not be used.

sources: Lewis & Short: diploma · Lewis & Short: licentia
